widgets_values:
Exercise: histogram tracking (back-projection + meanShift/CamShift)

The classic color tracker: LEARN what the object looks like once, then FOLLOW it by color statistics alone. A magenta disc is drawn onto the photo at four positions (a synthetic 'video'; it also drifts and GROWS from radius 22 to 34). Frame 0 teaches the model: the disc region (a circle mask) is histogrammed in HSV hue x saturation with 'CV Histogram' (normalize 'peak = 255'). Each later frame is scored with 'CV Back Project' - bright where pixels match the disc's colors (see the heatmap preview) - and 'CV Track Window' climbs that density from the PREVIOUS frame's window (min_density 32 so a few stray matching pixels never count as a lock): meanShift (red box, fixed 90x90) just follows position; CamShift (green box) also fits the size and angle, so its box grows with the disc. This whole per-frame recipe (score, both trackers, boxes) is a reusable 'Track a frame' subgraph instanced once per frame - open it to see the inner wiring. The window output chains frame -> frame as an NPARRAY; the first frame is seeded by a 'CV Scalar' (x, y, w, h) literal. The bbox output is core BOUNDING_BOX data - frame 3 is also rendered by the core 'Draw BBoxes' node.

ROBUSTNESS (do this on your own footage): a pixel's HUE is meaningless where saturation or value is low - near-gray and near-black pixels get an essentially random hue. So BOTH the learn step and every score step first build an S/V validity mask with 'inRange' (any hue, S>=80, V>=40) and AND it in: the model is learned only from trustworthy pixels (this is what saves you when your sample mask is sloppy and clips some background, or the object has an antialiased/shadowed rim - otherwise the histogram learns the background color and lights the whole frame), and each frame's back-projection is gated the same way before tracking.

RED OBJECTS / the hue wrap-around: red sits at BOTH ends of the hue circle (0 and 179). It still works here because we back-project a histogram LEARNED FROM THE OBJECT - it captures both ends, so the object lights up fully. The trap is only if you hand-pick a single hue BAND (e.g. inRange hue 0..10): red then needs TWO bands. Learning the histogram sidesteps that; so does tracking in the seam-free CIELab a*/b* plane if you ever need it.

FAILURE PATH (bottom): a window seeded at (700, 700) lies outside the 640x480 frame - an object that left the view. 'CV Track Window' reports found=false and echoes the window unchanged instead of raising (a lost track is a valid result, not an error); the if/else passes the unannotated frame through.
